name: Lobby Bar at Hotel Chelsea
take: Marble bar, chandelier, cheetah-print chairs and a serious martini: the hotel bar Chelsea goes to when it wants to feel expensive without a dress code.
theCatch: Cocktails start around $25 and the house martini is capped at two per person; ask for the garden room.
notes: Opened 2022 in the restored Hotel Chelsea; open daily 11am-2am, reservations on Resy with walk-ins at the bar. The Infatuation (Feb 2026) puts cocktails at $25-32 and notes the tableside martini is limited to two per guest. Fern-lined garden room off the main bar; El Quijote and Cafe Chelsea share the building for dinner.

name: Jungle Bird
take: Tropical drinks on 8th Avenue without the tiki costume: two floors, leather booths, and a room that stays social right up to closing.
theCatch: Early-bird cocktail deals run weekdays until 7; book the upstairs Canopy Room if you're more than six.
notes: Two floors with a bar on each, capacity about 190; the upstairs Canopy Room is bookable for parties. Open 3pm-2am Sun-Wed and until 3am Thu-Sat; early-bird specials Mon-Fri until 7pm plus a late-night food menu. Reservations on Resy; cocktails around $17.

name: La Noxe
take: A buzzer on 28th Street, a staircase into the subway station, and a red velvet lounge the size of a studio that turns into a disco by 11.
theCatch: Reserve for anything before 10:30; after that it's walk-in only and mostly standing.
notes: Entrance is a buzzer at 162 W 28th St; the room sits inside the 28th St 1 train station with a side exit back into the station. Open 6pm-1am Sun-Wed, 6pm-2am Thu-Sat; reservations on OpenTable, walk-ins after about 10:30pm when it shifts to a small dance floor. Six bar stools plus velvet couches; a second location opened at 111 Broadway.

name: Sid Gold's Request Room
take: Piano karaoke in a back room done up like a seventies Vegas lounge; you hand the pianist a request and the whole bar sings the chorus.
theCatch: Two-drink minimum, no cover, closed Sundays; reserve on Tock and tip the pianist.
notes: Front bar plus a back room where live piano karaoke runs six nights a week: Mon-Wed 9pm-1am, Thu-Fri 6pm-1am, Sat 9pm-1am; closed Sunday. Two-drink minimum and no cover; happy hour Wed-Fri 5-7pm takes $2 off wine and well drinks. Sister rooms in Detroit, Nashville and DC.

name: The Eagle
take: Chelsea's leather bar: three floors of dark rooms, a roof deck that runs until 4am, and a crowd that dressed for it, or didn't.
theCatch: Doors at 10pm most nights and dead before midnight; the roof is the summer move.
notes: Three floors with a roof deck and a full bar on each level, between 10th and 11th on W 28th. Open 10pm-4am Tue-Sat (Mon until 3am), Sun 5pm-4am, roof weather permitting. Leather and fetish crowd but jeans and t-shirts are fine; a gear shop occupies the freight elevator. Coat check $4; 21+ with government ID.

name: Trailer Park Lounge
take: Christmas lights, Elvis, a fake trailer built into the wall and strawberry margaritas: the cheap, silly bar every group eventually ends up at.
theCatch: Happy hour 4-7 daily; the tater tots are the order, and it gets loud after 10 on weekends.
notes: Kitsch bar on 23rd between 7th and 8th; Time Out lists noon-2am Sun-Wed and noon-4am Thu-Sat. Happy hour 4-7pm daily with the strawberry margarita as the house drink; fried food in baskets, tater tots, sweet potato fries. Takes private party bookings for big groups.

name: Peter McManus Cafe
take: Family-run since 1936 and open until 4am: oak bar, phone booths, Guinness, a good burger, and nobody has redecorated on purpose.
theCatch: Kitchen runs until midnight (1am Thu-Sat); the back dining room is the easier seat when the front fills.
notes: Opened 1936 at 7th Ave and 19th St and still run by the McManus family (Jamo McManus today). Open daily noon-4am; kitchen until midnight Sun-Wed and 1am Thu-Sat. The burger has won Battle of the Burger twice; the stained-glass back bar has a bullet hole in it. Two vintage phone booths; frequent film and TV location (Seinfeld, Law & Order, Broad City).

name: Smithfield Hall
take: The soccer bar: eleven screens behind the bar, a projector for the main match, pitchers on the table and a room that fills for 10am kickoffs.
theCatch: Big matches pack it early; email ahead if you need a specific game on the projector.
notes: Soccer-first sports bar on 25th between 6th and 7th, a few blocks from MSG. Eleven TVs behind the bar plus a pull-down projector for the featured match; shows leagues worldwide and will put a requested match on with notice. Tavern ale by the pitcher (about $24 per The Infatuation, July 2026); brunch, lunch and dinner menus; private events.

name: Frying Pan
take: A rusted lightship and a railroad barge on the Hudson where you drink buckets of beer at picnic tables and watch the sun drop behind New Jersey.
theCatch: Seasonal, roughly May to October and weather-dependent; the beer garden is first-come, the decks take reservations.
notes: Pier 66 at W 26th St in Hudson River Park, three blocks north of Chelsea Piers; the 1930s Lightship Frying Pan moored beside a Lackawanna railroad barge. Open daily from 11:30am in season (about May-October), closing time varies with weather. Full-service main deck and sundeck take reservations (parties up to 24); the beer garden is order-at-the-bar, first-come. Burgers, seafood, cocktails, beer buckets; Sunday three-course supper $48, Wednesday mussels-and-fries $22.

name: The Standard Biergarten
take: German beer, brats and ping-pong under the High Line; the one Meatpacking spot where twelve people in sneakers is the intended use.
theCatch: Weekend afternoons fill fast; it's heated and covered in winter, so don't write it off in January.
notes: Street-level beer garden under the High Line at Washington and 13th, entrance on Little W 12th. Posted winter hours: 3-11pm Mon-Wed, 2-11pm Thu, 2pm-2am Fri, noon-2am Sat, noon-11pm Sun; open-air in summer, heated in winter. German beers (Ayinger, Koestritzer), brats, currywurst, pretzels; ping-pong tables and picnic-table seating; Stammtisch tables reservable by email. Runs US Open viewing and Oktoberfest programming each fall.

name: Le Bain
take: The Standard's rooftop disco: a hot tub in the middle of the dance floor, a wraparound terrace over the Hudson, and a door that judges.
theCatch: Book on Resy if you're a group; come at sunset for the view and stay only if you want the club.
notes: Top floor of The Standard, High Line: two levels with an indoor dance floor, a plunge pool/jacuzzi, and an open-air roof with Hudson and skyline views. Hours Mon-Tue 4pm-midnight, Wed-Fri 4pm-4am, Sat 2pm-4am, Sun 2pm-midnight; 21+, reservations on Resy. DJ programming most nights including Eli Escobar's Wednesday party. In Time Out's Feb 2026 rooftop list.

name: Somewhere Nowhere
take: Thirty-nine floors up with a rooftop pool and skyline on every side; jazz and martinis early, then a bottle-service DJ room after 10.
theCatch: Go before 10pm when there's no cover; after that it's reservations and a $100 minimum.
notes: Floors 38-39 of the Renaissance New York Chelsea on 25th between 6th and 7th; indoor lounge with dance floor plus an open-air rooftop pool deck, igloos in winter. Hours Wed 5pm-1am, Thu noon-11pm, Fri-Sun noon-4am; closed Mon-Tue. Weekly program: Wednesday jazz, Thu-Fri 5-7pm martini hour, Friday comedy and Sinatra sets; DJs and bottle service from 10pm with mandatory reservations and a $100 minimum late.

name: Brass Monkey
address: 55 Little W 12th St, New York, NY 10014
take: The un-Meatpacking Meatpacking bar: a pub with a long tap list, burgers, a roof terrace and no rope, open past 2 on weekends.
theCatch: The roof terrace goes first on warm nights; Sunday it shuts at 10.
notes: Open since 2004 on Little W 12th between Washington and 10th; three indoor bars, a sidewalk cafe and a roof terrace. Posted hours roughly Mon 1pm-midnight, Tue-Wed noon-1am, Thu noon-2am, Fri-Sat noon-3am, Sun 1pm-10pm. Rotating drafts plus a long bottle list; burgers, brisket, bangers and mash, weekend brunch; TVs for games.

name: Rebar
take: Chelsea's mainstream gay dance bar, in the old G Lounge space: a proper layout, DJs, and weekend parties that actually fill the floor.
theCatch: Weeknights are calm; the weekend dance parties are the point.
notes: Opened 2017 at 225 W 19th (between 7th and 8th) in the former G Lounge; ownership passed to a group including Juan Boria in December 2024 and it remains open. Lounge layout with weekend DJ dance parties. Current hours were not confirmed online at time of research.

name: El Quijote
take: The 1930 Spanish room in the Hotel Chelsea, restored rather than reinvented: garlic shrimp, paella for the table, and a bar you can eat at alone.
theCatch: Book on Resy for a booth, or aim for a bar seat and finish next door at the Lobby Bar.
notes: Spanish restaurant and cocktail lounge open since 1930 in the Hotel Chelsea, renovated and reopened in 2022 with the Don Quijote glasswork and soldier murals kept. Tapas, pan con tomate, gambas al ajillo, seasonal seafood paella, Basque cheesecake; leather booths and bar seating. Reservations on Resy with slots running to 11pm; Infatuation 8.2/10.

name: Café Chelsea
take: Mirrors on every wall, tables close enough to hear the next one, and a $48 steak frites: the Hotel Chelsea brasserie built for watching people.
theCatch: Prime-time Resy slots go fast; the booth-lined bar area is the fallback, and breakfast is the easy way in.
notes: French-American brasserie inside the Hotel Chelsea in a former bait-and-tackle storefront, opened 2023. Art Deco room with mirrored walls, booths in the bar area, dining rooms hung with the hotel's art collection. Serves breakfast through dinner; hangar steak frites about $48, maitake au poivre, pain perdu. Reservations on Resy for parties up to 8; Infatuation 8.3/10.

name: Shukette
take: Loud, bread-obsessed Levantine cooking on 9th Avenue: fish grilled in a wire cage, za'atar lafa, tahini soft serve, and a table that wants six of you.
theCatch: Reservations are a fight and walk-in waits run one to two hours; the bar is the shortcut for two.
notes: Sister to Shuka in Soho, on 9th Ave at 24th St. Levantine menu built around bread (garlic frena, za'atar lafa), Fish In A Cage (whole porgy with green charmoula), joojeh chicken, shuk small plates, tahini soft serve. Resy reservations are hard to get and walk-in waits often run 1-2 hours; bar seating. Infatuation 8.1/10.

name: Pastis
take: The revived Meatpacking brasserie: subway tile, distressed mirrors, steak frites, and a crowd that treats dinner as the pre-game for wherever it's going next.
theCatch: Big and reservation-driven; the zinc bar is the walk-in play, and the room is loud by 8.
notes: Keith McNally's brasserie, originally opened 1999, closed 2014, reopened 2019 with Starr Restaurants in a larger space at Gansevoort and Greenwich. Dinner 5-11pm Sun-Thu, 5pm-midnight Fri-Sat, plus breakfast, lunch and weekend brunch. Curved zinc bar, subway tile, mirrored specials boards; escargots, moules frites $29, steak tartare, filet $68. Reservations on Resy; private events up to 50.

name: Los Mariscos
take: Baja fish tacos, aguachile and micheladas at picnic tables under Christmas lights, with its own 15th Street door so you skip the market crowd.
theCatch: Closes at 9 (8 on Sundays), so it's the early dinner before the Tippler, not the late one.
notes: Sister restaurant to Los Tacos No. 1, at the 9th Ave end of Chelsea Market with a separate entrance on W 15th St. Fish and shrimp tacos on handmade tortillas, ceviche tostadas, aguachile, a raw bar with oysters and clams; palomas, micheladas, margaritas and beer at a small bar with a TV; picnic-table seating and an open kitchen. Time Out lists 11am-9pm Mon-Sat, 11am-8pm Sun. Infatuation 8.5/10.
